newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Ikeda says China normal after Deng death.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Ikeda says China normal after Deng death.

text.p: Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda told U.S. Secretary of State Madeline Albright on Sunday there were no signs of "confusion" developing in China since the death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping last week.
The fact that China was accepting Albright's visit on Monday was proof of China's stability, a Japanese Foreign Ministry official quoted Ikeda as telling Albright.
"There appear to be no signs of confusion developing in China after Mr Deng's death," Ikeda said.
Albright, who leaves Tokyo for Beijing on Monday, told Ikeda she planned to raise a wide range of issues, from human rights to trade, during her two-day visit to China, the official said.

Ikeda said Japan was aware of the importance of the human rights issue in China and agreed with the United States that China needed to respect the law if the reformist line set by Deng was to be maintained.
Ikeda told Albright it was also important that Beijing allow Hong Kong to maintain its role as a key financial centre when the British colony reverts to China at the end of June.
Albright arrived in Tokyo on Sunday from Seoul as part of a nine-nation tour, her first overseas visit since becoming secretary of state last month.
Albright has also held talks with trade minister Shinji Sato and defence chief Fumio Kyuma and is to meet Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto over breakfast on Monday before leaving for Beijing.
